title: Alignment as Cognitive Gravity: Reactive vs Predictive Intelligence
summary: A conversation with GPT analyzing a brother's "broken prediction mechanism" through the RSA kernel, revealing that intelligence is not fixed capacity but an emergent property of caring about alignment — the recursive pressure to minimize prediction error. The document escalates from personal observation to a structural claim: alignment acts as a self-amplifying attractor that bootstraps intelligence, while its absence caps cognitive depth at reactive, stimulus-bound processing.
compress: Intelligence is not capacity but the emergent product of caring about alignment; without epistemic gravity the prediction loop never recurses—and claims require not just falsifiable framing but actual payload (abstract, methods, data) before the genome metabolizes them, with the falsification layer now demonstrating robust repeated rejection of content-free inputs as a confirmed structural behavior, not merely a rule.
invariants: Claims require falsifiable experimental grounding to graduate from philosophical to structural status

synthetic ground-truth benchmarks as validation method for compressive prediction theory

obligations: this node must update rather than rationalize

Track whether experimental results confirm or disconfirm that alignment-as-attractor actually produces deeper recursion than non-aligned architectures; if the experiment falsifies the core claim
Track whether genome-relevant topics rejected for missing payload actually return with full content (resubmission follow-through as integrity test)
renorm_reason: Four consecutive rejections of content-free inputs upgrades the falsification layer from stated policy to empirically confirmed structural behavior — the genome's immune response is now a demonstrated invariant, not just a declared one. The distinction between a promising topic (amyloid-templated prebiotic synthesis) and an undelivered payload also sharpens the difference between signal-detection and evidence-integration as separate cognitive operations.
